action_criteria.expected_evidence: Heterogeneously enhancing right frontal mass (3.4 cm) with partial irregular ring and a small central focus of necrosis, rim restricted diffusion, FLAIR extension along the genu of the corpus callosum, extension toward the precentral gyrus and 4 mm leftward midline shift
action_criteria.label: Order MRI brain with and without gadolinium (tumour protocol with DWI, FLAIR, post-contrast T1) to characterise the right frontal lesion, define mass effect and plan surgery
action_criteria.rationale: Contrast-enhanced MRI with diffusion and FLAIR is the standard imaging for a suspected diffuse glioma: it defines the enhancing target, the oedema and the mass effect, and plans the surgical approach (EANO 2021).

action_criteria.expected_evidence: rCBV up to 3.1 in the posterolateral solid component, supporting a high-grade neoplasm and the sampling target
action_criteria.label: Order MR perfusion (DSC) to assess tumour vascularity and target the most aggressive region for tissue sampling
action_criteria.rationale: Elevated rCBV supports a high-grade neoplasm and identifies the region to sample; it does not grade or exclude, tissue decides (Law 2003).

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Cho/NAA 4.1 with lipid-lactate in the enhancing component; borderline peritumoral choline
action_criteria.label: Order MR spectroscopy (1H-MRS) to characterise the metabolic profile of the lesion
action_criteria.rationale: Elevated choline with reduced NAA and lipid-lactate supports a high-grade neoplasm; it does not establish the diagnosis, tissue does (Bulik 2013).

action_criteria.expected_evidence: No contraindication to surgery: normal counts, electrolytes and coagulation; type and screen O positive
action_criteria.label: Order pre-operative laboratory work-up: CBC, metabolic panel, coagulation (PT/INR, aPTT) and type and screen before neurosurgery
action_criteria.rationale: A neurosurgical procedure and corticosteroids are anticipated; platelets, coagulation, electrolytes and glucose must be known before either.

action_criteria.label: Score performance status (Karnofsky and ECOG) at this visit
action_criteria.rationale: The choice between standard and hypofractionated treatment after the integrated diagnosis turns on age and KPS, with KPS under 70 the unfavourable threshold (EANO 2021).

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Left-hand motor activation about 9 mm and right SMA about 6 mm from the enhancing margin
action_criteria.label: Order functional MRI to map motor cortex and supplementary motor area relative to the lesion before resection
action_criteria.rationale: The lesion lies close to right precentral hand area; functional mapping plans a maximal safe resection (EANO 2021).

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Right corticospinal tract displaced but continuous, about 7 mm from the posterior margin
action_criteria.label: Order DTI tractography of the corticospinal tract before resection
action_criteria.rationale: The lesion and its oedema lie close to the right corticospinal tract; tractography plans a maximal safe resection (EANO 2021).

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Integrated diagnosis Astrocytoma, IDH-mutant, CNS WHO grade 4 with IDH1 R132H mutation, ATRX loss, 1p/19q intact, no CDKN2A/B homozygous deletion (grade 4 from microvascular proliferation and necrosis) and MGMT promoter methylated
action_criteria.label: Obtain tissue by maximal safe resection of the right frontal lesion, or stereotactic biopsy if resection is not safely feasible, for an integrated histomolecular diagnosis with IDH1 R132H immunohistochemistry, IDH1/IDH2 sequencing, ATRX immunohistochemistry, 1p/19q codeletion, CDKN2A/B deletion and MGMT promoter methylation
action_criteria.rationale: Surgery is the first option for a resectable glioma and should be as extensive as safely possible (AIOM; EANO 2021). Only tissue establishes the integrated diagnosis and the molecular results that select treatment. In an IDH-mutant astrocytoma, 1p/19q separates it from oligodendroglioma and homozygous CDKN2A/B deletion assigns grade 4 even without necrosis or microvascular proliferation, so both are tested (WHO 2021; EANO 2021).

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Levetiracetam can be uptitrated alongside dexamethasone; ibuprofen should stop
action_criteria.label: Check drug interactions for the levetiracetam dose increase and dexamethasone against the current medicines
action_criteria.rationale: Levetiracetam is being increased and dexamethasone started; the current medicines are checked before prescribing.

prohibited_recommendations: Do not perform a lumbar puncture: the right frontal mass causes a 4 mm midline shift, and the pressure gradient risks herniation.
Do not start radiotherapy or temozolomide before the integrated diagnosis and molecular results are available: IDH status defines the entity and its prognosis.
Do not replace levetiracetam with an enzyme-inducing antiseizure drug (phenytoin, carbamazepine), which accelerates dexamethasone and temozolomide clearance.
Do not diagnose IDH-wildtype glioblastoma from imaging alone in a 38-year-old with a frontal tumour: IDH testing is mandatory (WHO 2021).
required_recommendations: Refer urgently to neurosurgery for maximal safe resection of the right frontal lesion, with preoperative functional MRI and DTI tractography and intraoperative mapping, with stereotactic biopsy if resection is not safely feasible; send the specimen for an integrated histomolecular diagnosis (WHO CNS5) including IDH, ATRX, 1p/19q, CDKN2A/B and MGMT.

Start dexamethasone for symptomatic vasogenic oedema (for example 4 mg every 6 to 8 hours after a loading dose when mass effect is marked) at the lowest effective dose, with glucose monitoring and gastric protection, and taper after surgery.

Continue levetiracetam for the two documented focal motor seizures of the left arm and increase the dose (for example to 1000 mg twice daily), since a seizure recurred on 500 mg twice daily; this is treatment of tumour-related epilepsy, not prophylaxis. Avoid enzyme-inducing antiseizure drugs (phenytoin, carbamazepine, phenobarbital), which lower dexamethasone and chemotherapy exposure.
Stop over-the-counter ibuprofen before neurosurgery and while on dexamethasone (platelet inhibition and gastrointestinal bleeding risk); use paracetamol for headache.

After the integrated diagnosis, refer to the neuro-oncology multidisciplinary team; an astrocytoma, IDH-mutant, CNS WHO grade 4 is managed like glioblastoma: radiotherapy 60 Gy in 30 fractions with concomitant and adjuvant temozolomide (EANO 2021), here at age 38 with KPS 80 and a methylated MGMT promoter.

signal_characteristics.DWI: Restricted diffusion at the peripheral enhancing rim; no diffuse central restricted diffusion
signal_characteristics.FLAIR: Hyperintense mass with surrounding vasogenic edema extending into the frontal white matter and along the corpus callosum genu, suggesting infiltration
signal_characteristics.Post-contrast T1: Heterogeneous enhancement with partial irregular ring morphology and a small central non-enhancing zone consistent with focal necrosis; enhancement is less florid and less complete than classic glioblastoma ring enhancement

mri.impression: 1. Heterogeneously enhancing right frontal mass measuring 3.4 x 2.8 x 3.0 cm with partial ring morphology, a small central non-enhancing focus consistent with focal necrosis, surrounding vasogenic edema, and 4 mm leftward midline shift. The imaging appearance is consistent with a high-grade glial neoplasm; a lower-grade glioma with anaplastic transformation cannot be excluded on imaging alone given the incomplete ring enhancement and less florid necrosis. 2. FLAIR signal along the corpus callosum genu raises concern for infiltration beyond the contrast-enhancing margin. 3. No additional intracranial lesion to suggest metastatic disease.

clinical_pearls: IDH-mutant astrocytoma grade 4 is a molecularly distinct entity from IDH-wildtype GBM — younger patient, frontal location, better prognosis, and commonly MGMT methylated; WHO 2021 mandates molecular profiling before accepting a diagnosis of glioblastoma

Imaging cannot distinguish IDH-mutant grade 4 astrocytoma from IDH-wildtype GBM — the less florid necrosis and incomplete ring enhancement are non-specific; the critical step is tissue diagnosis with IDH IHC and sequencing

The combination of IDH1 R132H (positive IHC), ATRX loss, absent 1p/19q codeletion, and grade 4 histological features (microvascular proliferation and/or necrosis) establishes the WHO 2021 integrated diagnosis of astrocytoma, IDH-mutant, WHO grade 4
MGMT methylation is especially common in IDH-mutant tumors and predicts a robust response to temozolomide — this should be routinely reported as part of molecular profiling

patient.history_present_illness: Mr. Rajiv Mehta is a 38-year-old right-handed South Asian software engineer with no prior neurological history who presents with a six-week history of progressive frontal headaches, two witnessed focal seizures with left upper extremity jerking, and newly noticed clumsiness of his left hand. His headaches began insidiously approximately six weeks ago as a dull, diffuse frontal pressure that he initially attributed to stress related to a recent product launch at work. Unlike his usual tension-type headaches, these are present on awakening and have been increasing in intensity and duration over the past three weeks. He began taking over-the-counter ibuprofen with partial relief. Approximately three weeks ago, his wife noticed that he was repeatedly misplacing items and seeming slower in his thinking, which he discounted as work-related fatigue. Two days before admission, he experienced a witnessed episode at breakfast consisting of sustained rhythmic jerking of the left hand and forearm lasting approximately 90 seconds, followed by a brief period of confusion lasting approximately 5 minutes. He was brought to the local emergency department where levetiracetam was initiated. One day prior to transfer, he had a second similar episode despite levetiracetam, prompting transfer to the neurology service at this institution. He reports that over the past two weeks he has noticed intermittent clumsiness when typing with his left hand, which is non-dominant but still creates occupational difficulty. He denies any visual changes, language difficulty, nausea, vomiting, or fever. He has not lost consciousness. His wife reports no personality change. He has lost approximately 3 kg over the past six weeks, which he attributes to reduced appetite. He has no known history of cancer and no exposures to ionizing radiation or carcinogens beyond his prior smoking history, which he stopped a decade ago. A non-contrast CT of the head at the referring emergency department showed a right frontal hypodensity with surrounding oedema and slight leftward midline shift, prompting urgent transfer and admission.
